transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. What brings you into the clinic today?
I’ve been having trouble keeping my head clear at work. I lose track of what clients are saying, reread the same chart note over and over, and then just freeze on simple decisions I used to handle.
When did you first start noticing these difficulties with your focus and decision-making?
About a month now. It started around when the clinic lost staff and I got shifted to late-evening coverage with a lot more crisis paperwork.
Over the past month, have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day?
I’m not really sure. I’ve mostly noticed the trouble concentrating at work.
Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in activities you normally enjoy?

Yeah. My guitar’s just been sitting in the corner, and I keep bailing on soccer and volunteering at the shelter. Even when I try to cook or go hiking, it feels like I’m just going through the motions—like there’s no point to it.
How has your sleep been over the past month?
I get home exhausted, but then I lie awake for hours replaying the day. And when I do finally fall asleep, I wake up before my alarm feeling like I barely slept.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite over the past month?
Yeah, I’ve barely been feeling hungry most days. I’ll skip meals without really meaning to unless someone reminds me, and my pants have started fitting loose.
Over the past month, have you been experiencing feelings of worthlessness or feeling like you are letting everyone down?
Yeah. If I miss even one detail in a note or don’t return a call right away, I start telling myself I’m useless—that I’m letting the clients and everyone at the clinic down.
Have you been experiencing persistent fatigue or a lack of energy throughout the day?
Yeah. Even small things, like showering, driving to the clinic, or finishing paperwork, feel like I’m dragging around a backpack full of bricks.
With everything feeling so heavy, have you had any thoughts of death, dying, or hurting yourself?
I don’t have a plan to hurt myself, but… I keep thinking it might be easier if I just didn’t wake up. That scares me, because I know what those thoughts can mean.

Symptoms have persisted for approximately one month and cause marked functional impairment at work and in daily life.

Recurrent thoughts of death and passive suicidal ideation
